setlist.title: It's All Over Now, Baby Blue

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Valley Road** (3 reviews): Called the best version of Valley Road the reviewer has heard the band play; Old Valley Road was the main reason the reviewer decided to get off the bus after this show [15][19][21]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Reviewer attended; the lighting during The Other One was mind-blowing, and the performance was a beast; Brutal, fast, unforgiving Other One; reviewer ranks it a top-ten version, alongside April 1 1988 [12][18]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Vinnie's playing on Bird Song convinced the reviewer he belonged with the band [21]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Relaxed, easy pace, with lovely keyboard work by Bruce on Eyes [15]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Wharf Rat is singled out as kicking royally [13]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Lovelight is hot and feels like a summary of the whole show in one song [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Valley Road**: rare: 7 archived performances [23]

## The recordings

- **gd90-12-04.sbd.ladner.9365.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 178 min; rated 3.8/5 by 10 [1]. Said about its sound: Full, rich soundboard sound typical of the period, with Bruce's keyboard playing adding a nice touch; Opening parts have shaky, unmixed sound; the rest of the soundboard recording rocks; Nice rich sound from the soundboard [11][13][15]
- **gd1990-12-04.143584.sbd.ebel.flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 183 min [2]
- **gd1990-12-04.143517.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 21 songs; 179 min [3]
- **gd1990-12-04.143441.DSBD.Reutelhuber.Westcott.Noel.t-flac1648**: soundboard; 21 songs; 184 min [4]
- **gd1990-12-04.beyer-m160.d5scott.105425.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 167 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [8]. Said about its sound: Described as a decent capture [19]

## Around the show

- Show marked the 25th anniversary of the band's first show as the Grateful Dead on 12/04/65; earlier they were the Warlocks [12]
- Reviewer wonders whether the band knew it was their silver anniversary; Phil's commanding presence is praised [13]
- Legend says the band dosed heavily; there was an unspoken acknowledgment it was their 25th birthday show [14]
- Reviewer agrees with another commenter that the lighting on one song was exceptional [14]
- Recording can't capture the room: energy rolled across the floor and people glowed in the dark at the Oakland Coliseum [17]
- Reviewer had seen about ten or twelve shows before this one and over 150 after it [18]
- Reviewer held tickets for all three McNichols nights but chose this outdoor-ish Oakland show for a warm December venue instead [19]
- Huey Lewis played harmonica on the encore [2]
- The previous night was the reviewer's first show after Brent and wasn't impressive; this night erased doubts [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd90-12-04.sbd.ladner.9365.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>DAT>CDR>WAV>SHN [1]. Also: Soundboard to DAT to CDR; Me & My Uncle and Big River come from an audience or matrix-like source; Source circulated via neolevo and candyman ftp in April 2002 [1]
- **gd1990-12-04.143584.sbd.ebel.flac1644**: transferred by Pete Ebel; source: Soundboard (Ultra-Matrix?) -> DAT [2]. Also: Four soundboard Ultra-Matrix sources appear to share one feed; this one has soundboard for the entire show, including Me & My Uncle and Big River; Early DAT copies had audience source for Me & My Uncle and Big River; Charlie's cassettes had soundboard [2]
- **gd1990-12-04.143517.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644**: taped by Don Pearson; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/TDK SA-X100) [3]. Also: Two sets of masters were combined to complete the show; this file set is 16-bit/44.1 kHz [3]
- **gd1990-12-04.143441.DSBD.Reutelhuber.Westcott.Noel.t-flac1648**: taped by Bill Reutelhuber; transferred by Joe Noel and Kris Wescott; source: Digital Soundboard > DAT (clone) [4]
- **gd1990-12-04.beyer-m160.d5scott.105425.flac16**: taped by D5scott; transferred by D5scott; source: Two Beyer M160 Mics > Sony TC-D5M 25 feet from stage - center - mics @ 5.5 feet high on a stand > analog cassette master [8]
